points.quote: the same shading calculation applied to different inputs
points.problem: "Shading" is never explained anywhere earlier in the book, yet the GPU's whole motivation (and Fig 16.6's 'shading 64 pixels') rests on it; a newcomer cannot tell what is being computed per pixel.
points.hint: Gloss in a few words, e.g. working out each pixel's colour.

points.quote: including the states the designer assumed were impossible
points.problem: Closing sentence restates the paragraph as an aphorism (law 2 and the AI-prose rule). Also 'hardware interlocks' and 'state machine' are used unglossed.
points.hint: End on the Therac facts or cut the closer; gloss interlock as a hardware safety stop.

points.quote: A cache built for speed is also a channel an attacker can time
points.problem: Aphorism closer that only restates the preceding sentences.

The caption and paragraph name the four states but never say what 'modified' or 'exclusive' mean; the figure shows 'A supplies, writes back' with no account of why a write-back is needed (memory is stale), so the newcomer must infer the states from the animation alone.
points.hint: One clause defining M (changed here, memory out of date) and E (the only copy, unchanged).
